To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of a two-stage sampling plan employing the county as the primary sampling unit and a ratio estimator of the form (x/y), where x is the mean of the variable of interest in the sample and y is the mean of a related variable for the same sample units, provides estimates that are unbiased, have small sampling errors, and can be computed quickly.

(i) a two-stage sampling design employing the county as a primary sampling unit is an efficient method of securing state level estimates of farm production and (ii) a ratio estimator is a more efficient method of estimation than a direct estimator.
the ratio estimate of the average of all counties in the state is a better estimate than the average of all primary sampling units.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the application of two-stage sampling to the preparation of state level estimates of agricultural items.
the application of various survey designs and estimation procedures to the preparation of state estimates.
the development of a sampling design for the preparation of state estimates in the field of agricultural statistics which is both efficient and practical.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ratio estimate of the total is the most accurate of the eight estimates considered.
the ratio estimate of a sub-sampling design using the county as a primary sampling unit is the preferred estimator for the state total.
the ratio estimate is superior to all other estimates examined.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of the county as a primary sampling unit is a practical and efficient method for obtaining state estimates.
the ratio estimator is the best of the methods examined.
the ratio estimate, using the ratio of the sample mean to the population mean of the auxiliary variable, is superior to the direct estimator in terms of efficiency.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the county is a very important unit in agricultural surveys and that the county should be used as a primary sampling unit.

the use of a two-stage sample design with probability proportional to county size for the first stage selection of primary sampling units (PSU) is a viable alternative to equal probability without loss in efficiency.
, for this particular application, the ratio estimate is a very efficient way of estimating the state total.
